items.summary: Asian stocks surged on Oct 27 as Anthropic’s US IPO filing lifted risk appetite ahead of tech earnings and central bank meetings. South Korea’s KOSPI gained more than 4% in early trading while Japan’s Nikkei was 1.9% higher, with the MSCI Asia-Pacific index up 1.2%. Meta Platforms’ plan to raise up to US$95 billion also boosted sentiment. Analysts say investors want proof that AI demand is broadening beyond interconnected relationships before infrastructure expansion continues (Ameriprise). The US 10-year Treasury yield held steady at 4.992%, below the 5% it breached in September as investors sought safety amid AI-driven market volatility, Reuters reported.
items.title: Asian Stocks Rise on Anthropic IPO Filing and Central Bank Calendar

items.summary: A news roundup of Anthropic's prospectus highlights explosive but costly expansion: the firm reported $16.3bn in revenue with an $80 bn loss for the first half of 2026, though much came from a $72.4bn one-off charge. Executives describe ambitions likened to 'a country of geniuses in a datacenter' and note AI safeguards may be incomplete or circumvented. The filing also lays out 92 pages of business risks, including reliance on top executives and enterprise customers, US infrastructure concentration, regulatory exposure and evolving insurance coverage for AI liabilities.
items.title: Anthropic's S-1 filing draws four key takeaways on growth, risks and safeguards

items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast model for visual reasoning and computer use that replaces GPT-5.6 Terra in the API as gpt-6.1-terra. Standard pricing is $5 per million output tokens, half of GPT-6.1 Sol's rate. On Agents' Last Exam v1 at medium effort, Terra scores 57.6% for $0.29 per task versus Astra's same score at $4.82. It reaches 85.5% on MMMU-Pro (Vision), within 1.2 points of GPT-6 Astra, but only solves 50.3% of Terminal-Bench 4.0 coding tasks, trailing Sonnet 5.5's 70.6%. OpenAI reports the scores and notes production error rates will differ; weights are closed.
items.title: OpenAI Launches Cheaper Visual Reasoning Model GPT-6.1 Terra

items.summary: OpenAI released its always-on AI personal assistant, dots, at a developer day in late September, positioning it as this year’s answer to how people will use deep learning models. OpenAI enterprise product team lead Alexander Embiricos explained the product came from reframing the technology as an intuitive single conversation rather than many conversations. The assistant is available in ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps for Pro tier or higher subscribers on plans starting at $100 a month, and it proactively flags calendar conflicts and deadlines once connected to tools like email and computer. In testing, its ability to think ahead was useful but not yet timely enough.
items.title: How OpenAI turned its coding tools into dots, an always-on personal assistant

items.summary: Bob Michele, J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s head of global fixed income, said on Oct 27 that bond markets hold “a generational amount of yield” and urged buying US debt offering up to 8% over the next year. He noted yields rebounded after September and October sell-offs, with the Fed funds rate expected at 3.75% to 4%. The tail risk is a further hike beyond 4.5%.
items.title: J.P. Morgan Fixed Income Head Calls Bond Market a Buy

items.summary: Trillions of dollars have been wiped from China’s stock markets in recent months amid increasing anxiety about the future of artificial intelligence, as Beijing races against the United States for dominance. The STAR 50 Index has plunged 40% since June, while other major-company indexes dropped by about 20%. According to Bloomberg, the fall has wiped out $2.4tn from the Chinese stock market since May. AI stocks account for over 40% of value in China and Hong Kong, per Goldman Sachs. Dan Wang of the Eurasia Group cited weak domestic demand, rising US rates and profit-margin pressures as drivers, noting any optimism remains limited ahead of next year’s Party Congress.
items.title: Chinese Markets Lose Trillions Amid AI Race With US

items.summary: South Korean police identified seven suspects behind a cybercrime operation that breached more than 90 organizations, using the ARTEX AI pentesting framework in most attacks. The gang leader, a self-taught hacker with penetration testing experience from 2019 to 2022, stole 8.2 million records and demanded ransom of 360 million won ($270,000) across 38 incidents. Only the leader remains in custody; six suspects stay under investigation.
items.title: South Korea Arrests AI-Powered Cybercrime Gang Leader

items.summary: Heatmap reports Anthropic's more-than-330-page IPO filing devotes considerable space to power supply risks, with the word 'energy' appearing 14 times in its risk section. The company worries it may not secure enough electricity for data centers running its models and faces rising costs from energy price spikes.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO Filing Flags Data Center Power Risks

items.summary: The top executives of U.S. startup Polar LNG resigned in recent weeks, six months after the company launched, amid a controversy over alleged funding and control by Russia's Novatek. Former CEO Joel Riddle told the Financial Times he discovered Novatek was financing and directing the project without Treasury approval. The firm responded that Riddle was terminated for cause and is under investigation. Polar LNG targets natural gas deliveries by the end of 2030, subject to securing permits and financing. There has been no progress in obtaining an OFAC license to buy a GBS from Novatek.
items.title: Executives Resign at Polar LNG Over Alleged Russian Control

items.summary: BYD’s Yangwang sub-brand is preparing an ultra-luxury electric sedan, potentially debuting next week in the UAE. The model would feature Rolls-Royce-style coach doors and reportedly BYD’s first solid-state batteries. Local reports suggest a length of about 5,500 mm (216″) and megawatt flash charging support. Yangwang executives Hu Xiaoqing and Zheng Yu confirmed details remain limited, while Stella Li indicated the battery debut targets 2027. FinDreams plans sulfide-based all-solid-state production in 2027. Prices are rumored near $300,000.
items.title: BYD Signals Ultra-Luxury EV Debut With Solid-State Batteries

items.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz in February disrupted a large share of global oil and gas trade, hitting Asia hardest. Southeast Asian nations scrambled to fill supply gaps with a rapid solar boom, but grid infrastructure has not kept pace, stalling many renewable projects. A new McKinsey report estimates Asian nations may need $1 trillion annually over 15 years for energy security as demand rises sharply through 2040.
items.title: Asia Faces Trillion-Dollar Energy Investment Need After Hormuz Shock

items.summary: Instagram is testing long-form videos of up to 90 minutes through a new format called Features. The move aims to connect short-form discovery with longer viewing sessions and could support podcasts, interviews, and comedy shows. However, questions about monetisation, accessibility, and creator earnings remain unanswered.
items.title: Meta Tests Long-Form Video on Instagram, Raising Questions for YouTube

items.summary: Shares of Tata Motors Ltd rose after the firm said it had secured provisional acceptances covering 87.81% of Iveco Group’s share capital under its €3.91 billion (approximately Rs 42,561 crore) offer, meeting the minimum acceptance threshold and bringing completion closer. A filing dated October 27 reported that TML CV Holdings B.V. received provisional results showing shareholders tendered 238.16 million Iveco shares by the October 26 deadline.
items.title: Tata Motors Takeover Bid Crosses Iveco Acceptance Threshold

items.summary: Microsoft said on Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce. A source familiar with the matter told Reuters requesting anonymity that marketing, commercial business and security units would be excluded while AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices remain eligible. The move comes as Microsoft forecasts US$175 billion in capital expenditures for 2026 amid investor scrutiny over returns on its heavy spending on AI data centres and chips.
items.title: Microsoft Offers Buyouts to Contain Costs and Fund AI Spending

items.summary: On Monday, AI-linked stocks rose after Anthropic disclosed the paperwork for its initial public offering. Nvidia shares added nearly 3 per cent; Microsoft and Amazon each gained nearly 1 per cent. CoreWeave and Nebius Group climbed 5.7 per cent and 2.3 per cent respectively. Analysts say a pure-play AI flotation could reshape how markets value chipmakers and infrastructure firms, while diverting capital from some tech heavyweights.
items.title: AI Stocks Rise as Anthropic Nears Wall Street Debut Amid Investor Caution

items.summary: The piece argues that Abbott and Costello's "Who's on First?" skit is not simply stupid but can be read as a commentary on how the establishment exploits less-tutored immigrants without apology. It notes Costello was an Italian-American immigrant, while Abbott stood in for a commercialized establishment, with names like Broadhurst signaling that class. The author admits uncertainty—stating this interpretation "stands at least some chance of being funny" but is not itself funny—and acknowledges the skit plays on ethnic prejudice uncomfortably rather than only critiquing it.
items.title: A Second Reading of Who's on First

items.summary: As Chancellor John Healey prepares his first Budget amid borrowing costs at historic highs, BBC News reports how people across income levels want it to address their finances. Chloe, a single mother earning £41,000, limits her weekly shop to £40; Robert Portlock on £22,000 says saving for a house is impossible and wants fuel duty cut or the personal allowance raised to about £16,000 from £12,570. Dave Herbert spends around £350 monthly on petrol, up 40% to 50%, urging removal of fuel duty. Jonathan Whitwam on £150,000 welcomes higher taxes and a wealth tax above £10m; retired Christine Morris worries about standing charges and the triple lock's end in 2030.
items.title: UK Families Urge Healey's Budget on Fuel, Housing and Tax Burden

items.summary: Brazilian markets plunged Monday after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won reelection, as investors repositioned bets on challenger Flávio Bolsonaro. An analyst told Bloomberg the market would 'reprice everything,' and some $6 billion in corporate equity sales were derailed. Stocks had earlier surged over Bolsonaro's deficit-trim pledge, but both candidates promised costly subsidies amid rising public debt.
items.title: Brazilian Markets Plunge After Lula's Reelection Victory

items.summary: Democratic movements scored symbolic victories in Venezuela and Serbia on Sunday, but a political scientist warned both face structural obstacles to lasting change. María Corina Machado returned from nearly 10 months of exile after winning Venezuela's opposition leadership. In Serbia, student protesters ended the strongman leader's 14-year rule. Francis Fukuyama argued Serbia's movement succeeded by avoiding specific intentions, suggesting its win may be unsustainable.
items.title: Venezuela and Serbia Democratic Wins Face Structural Challenges

items.summary: US AI company Anthropic publicly filed its prospectus for an initial public offering on Monday that could become the largest stock market debut in history. The filing offers the first detailed look at the finances of the developer of the Claude models. Revenues reached $16.29 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $1.16 billion year on year. Anthropic recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion for the period, though most stemmed from accounting charges as its valuation climbed. The company warned that this rapid pace may not last and said it could not assure revenue would continue to grow.
items.title: Anthropic Files for Record-Breaking IPO, Reports Soaring Revenue and Large Losses

items.summary: The Ministry of Culture and Tourism said China's domestic tourism market grew solidly from January to September 2026, with more than 5.3 billion trips up 6.2% year on year. Urban residents made over 4 billion trips while rural residents took 1.27 billion. Spending rose 2.2% to 4.95 trillion yuan (about $737 billion). A five-year plan set targets of 8.3 billion trips and 7.7 trillion yuan by 2030.
items.title: China Reports Steady Growth in Domestic Tourism for First Nine Months

items.summary: A WhatsApp group called the Exército do Lula (Lula's Army), mobilised by congressman André Janones, grew to more than 10.8 million followers and is credited with flipping Brazil's election after Flávio Bolsonaro won an unexpected first-round victory on October 4 with 47 per cent of the ballot. The group urged young voters to turn out in person. In the second round held on October 25, Lula secured 51.8 per cent of the vote and became president for a fourth time.
items.title: WhatsApp Army Helped Lula Win Brazil's Second Round

items.summary: Anthropic disclosed plans on Monday (Oct 26) to sell shares in an initial public offering, according to The Wall Street Journal. Its filing reports sales of US$11.6 billion in the April-June quarter, up from US$787 million a year earlier, and its first operating profit near US$1 billion, though it still recorded an overall loss of US$80 billion for the first half of 2025. The company devotes over 90 pages to safety risks, warning that advanced systems could pose catastrophic or existential risks if not developed responsibly. It faces scrutiny after being barred by the Pentagon as a supplier under President Donald Trump's administration and committed billions to computing capacity with SpaceX, Amazon and Google. Analysts note growth may slow sharply before its planned debut the week of Nov 16.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO Filing Highlights AI Risks and Record Sales

items.summary: The foldable iPhone Duo, one of Apple's largest new products in years, is receiving a growing number of complaints that its display cracked within hours or days. Customers report hearing a crunching sound when unfolding the phone, followed by a crack along the center crease and sometimes a white patch on the right side. Reports first appeared on Reddit and other social media sites.
items.title: Apple's Foldable iPhone Duo Draws Screen-Cracking Complaints

items.summary: Anthropic is preparing what could become history's largest capital markets fundraising, potentially surpassing SpaceX's $US85.7 billion ($121 billion) listing in June 2025. The self-described AI safety company plans to raise about $US100 billion after analysts revalued it downwards from $US2 trillion to $US1.5 trillion. Third-quarter revenue rose to $US16 billion, with annualised run rate reportedly topping $US65 billion at end of July 2025. However, the company spent $US5.6 billion in one quarter on computing power while operating losses grow. Analysts note it has not yet produced numbers justifying its valuation and warns that if AI demand fails to justify spending, the entire trade risks collapse.
items.title: Anthropic's record IPO amid AI bubble fears

items.summary: Anthropic filed for its initial public offering Monday, poised as the first major U.S. firm focused solely on building AI software to debut publicly. The filing highlights astonishing growth alongside uncertainty about demand and spending needs. It shows billions in annual product sales but raises questions about extreme losses, profitability, government intervention, and catastrophic-harm risks specific to cutting-edge developers.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO Spotlight on AI Boom Extremes and Uncertainty

items.summary: A completion ceremony was held Saturday in Sinphyong County, North Hwanghae Province of the DPRK, marking renovation work on Chinese People's Volunteers (CPV) martyrs' cemeteries. The event coincided with the 76th anniversary of the CPV's entry into the DPRK during the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea. Representatives from China and the DPRK laid flower baskets, stood in silent tribute, presented flowers, poured liquor, and visited tombs and a wall of martyrs' names.
items.title: Completion ceremony held for renovated CPV martyrs' cemetery in DPRK

items.summary: A speech by Chinese President Xi Jinping at a ceremony marking the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March has been published as a booklet. Delivered in Beijing on October 22, it was issued by the People's Publishing House and is now available at Xinhua Bookstore outlets nationwide.
items.title: Xi Jinping Speech on Long March Published as Booklet

items.summary: The NFL announced that rapper Jay-Z will perform at the February halftime show, marking his first appearance despite Roc Nation producing it since 2019. The event follows Beyoncé and other recent performers like Bad Bunny and Kendrick Lamar, whose 2025 set was history's most watched. Jay-Z celebrates a 30th anniversary of Reasonable Doubt and holds 25 Grammy awards. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell expressed excitement about his cultural impact.
items.title: Jay-Z Confirmed as Super Bowl Halftime Headliner

items.summary: A localised ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump took effect early Tuesday in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, southern Ukraine. According to her office, she led talks with civilian negotiators from both countries after meeting UN officials who briefed her on conditions there. Up to 2,000 people remain stranded amid dwindling food and medicine. Minutes later, Kyiv faced a wave of Russian ballistic missile strikes that damaged infrastructure.
items.title: Ceasefire Begins in Oleshky as Kyiv Suffers Strikes

items.summary: Israeli polls opened for what many call the country's most consequential election, held three years after the 7 October Hamas attacks that killed about 1,200 people. Most polling suggests Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition will lose its majority in the 120-seat Knesset, though the opposition is also expected to fall short of forming a government.
items.title: Israel Opens Polls in Historic Election Expected to Topple Netanyahu Coalition

items.summary: An NPR guide explains Israel's Tuesday elections, which many Israelis call the most consequential in their country's history. Voters choose among a dozen parties for the 120-seat Knesset rather than between candidates directly, and party leaders must then build coalitions of at least 61 lawmakers. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu trails challenger Gadi Eisenkot in recent polls, though neither has a clear path to a majority. The vote centers on accountability for the October 7 Hamas-led attack that killed about 1,200 people, military service obligations, judicial power and international standing.
items.title: Israel's pivotal election pits Netanyahu against Eisenkot as coalition math remains uncertain

items.summary: On October 27, HSBC reported a 32 per cent surge in third-quarter profit on Tuesday as rate hikes supported net interest income. Pretax profit reached $9.6 billion for the July-September quarter. The bank also unveiled a share buyback of up to $1 billion and announced an interim dividend of $0.1 per share.
items.title: HSBC Reports Third-Quarter Profit Surge and Announces Share Buyback

items.summary: The Duchess of Sussex has been confirmed as a co-host of the new season of Junior MasterChef Australia, joining the 2027 series as a special guest alongside Poh Ling Yeow. The announcement follows her appearance as a guest judge on MasterChef Australia last year and comes amid renewed scrutiny over allegations involving Thomas Markle, whom she says broke contact with after learning he had abused young girls.
items.title: Meghan Confirmed as Co-Host of Junior MasterChef Australia

items.summary: Roy Sesana, a 97-year-old Indigenous rights campaigner who opposed the removal of San communities from Central Kalahari, received an honorary doctorate from the University of Botswana on Oct. 23. The university said the honor recognized “a lifetime of service that goes beyond individual achievement.” Sesana dedicated it to the Basarwa and people of Botswana, while noting the struggle for ancestral land remains unresolved.
items.title: Botswana Honors Elder Activist With Doctorate

items.summary: As the EU's deforestation regulation (EUDR) approaches enforcement after multiple delays, Mongabay's Solutions Desk is examining how industries are working to comply and where shortfalls remain. The Special Issue covers soy traders in Brazil, cocoa companies in Ghana, and palm oil farmers in Southeast Asia, identifying persistent challenges in data accuracy, supply chain complexity, and equity for smallholder farmers.
items.title: Mongabay Examines Who Is Implementing the EU Deforestation Regulation

items.summary: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer warned Monday that a $3.4 billion European Investment Bank loan to Airbus could jeopardise the tariff truce between Washington and Brussels, saying his office had received no details about the financing announced in June. He urged quick resolution and said it injects substantial uncertainty into transatlantic aerospace trade. The EIB described the record funding as aimed at research across commercial aviation and defence. (FRANCE 24 with AFP)
items.title: Trump Trade Official Warns EU Loan Threatens US-EU Truce

items.summary: Greek Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis said on Monday that a 2019 memorandum between Turkey and Libya over Mediterranean maritime boundaries remains null and void. Delivering a joint statement for Greece, Egypt, Cyprus, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and the European Union, he described it as contrary to international law and without legal effect. The signatories reaffirmed their commitment to Libyan reunification.
items.title: Greece reaffirms Turkey-Libya maritime deal is void under international law

items.summary: Vedika Bahl fact-checked three viral videos falsely presented as recent unrest across Europe amid protests over poor school conditions and rising living costs. One, viewed more than a million times on X, showed footage nearly nine years old from Poland’s 2017 Independence Day march. A second depicted military preparations in Porto for Army Day, not troop deployment against protesters; police handled demonstrations instead, arresting more than 30 people. The third traced to August in Buenos Aires, Argentina, with no link to Italy.
items.title: Fact-checkers Debunk Viral Videos of European Protests

items.summary: Human rights activists condemned the alleged abduction of Twaha Mwaipaya, a former Tanzanian opposition official jailed in 2022 and now in exile in Kenya. Amnesty International said he was taken by three vehicles while riding to visit friends near Nairobi on Sunday afternoon. Chadema's John Kitoka warned that such abductions may end in death. Amnesty urged authorities to establish his whereabouts, calling the pattern a growing trend of transnational repression.
items.title: Rights activists condemn alleged abduction of Tanzanian opposition figure in Kenya

items.summary: A news roundup reports Indian equity benchmark Nifty opening lower near 22,705 amid monthly options expiry. The rupee opened at 95.17 per dollar. Separately, AI company Anthropic filed to go public on NASDAQ under ticker ANT with a potential valuation of up to 2 trillion dollars and an 81 billion dollar first-half net loss. Other items cover Cyclone Arnab intensifying over the Bay of Bengal and political developments in Delhi.
items.title: Indian Markets Open Flat as Anthropic Files for IPO

items.summary: In an SEC registration statement filed on October 26, Anthropic warned that disruptions to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company’s operations could harm its business. The company said most advanced chip capacity is concentrated in Taiwan and exposed to natural disasters, geopolitical tensions with China, and infrastructure failures. It added that building replacement capacity outside Taiwan remains early-stage and may not reduce these risks soon.
items.title: Anthropic Flags TSMC Disruption Risk for AI Chips

items.summary: Tata Motors won decisive shareholder backing for its €3.91-billion takeover of Italian truckmaker Iveco, with investors representing 87.81 per cent of equity accepting the offer on Monday after overcoming minority resistance and clearing the biggest hurdle in its 15-month pursuit. The acquisition aims to build a global commercial-vehicle group with combined annual revenue of approximately €21 billion.
items.title: Tata Motors Secures Decisive Shareholder Backing for Iveco Takeover Deal

items.summary: On Monday, Instagram began testing new features aimed at long-form content creators such as podcasters and comedians in the US. The feature, called “Features,” lets users link short Reels to full-length videos. Tessa Lyons, vice-president of product at Instagram, described how viewers can continue watching after seeing a clip.
items.title: Instagram Tests 90-Minute Horizontal Videos for Long-Form Creators

items.summary: Anthropic filed an S-1 with the SEC on October 26, announcing a proposed initial public offering of Class A common stock. The company intends to list shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under ticker "ANT," though it has not set share count or price range. The filing is not yet effective; securities cannot be sold until then. Anthropic's announcement is neither an offer nor solicitation, and any sale would occur only through a prospectus available from Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC or Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC.
items.title: Anthropic Files for Nasdaq IPO Under ANT Ticker

items.summary: Microsoft's new voluntary exit offer, open to about 60,000 employees at level 70 and below in the US, Canada, India and the UK, is built on standard severance terms rather than a custom deal. GeekWire reports it covers base pay tied to tenure, continued stock vesting, healthcare for a fixed period and career transition services. A company spokesperson told KUOW that terms vary by market.
items.title: Microsoft's Voluntary Exit Package Mirrors Standard Severance Terms

items.summary: Netflix named Wilson, a former Apple Podcasts and Daylight Media executive, as an initial consultant to advance its podcasts. The streaming company confirmed the appointment while Wilson declined comment. It arrives after Netflix announced plans to cut 6% of its workforce this month, as it builds a foothold in podcasting despite heavy investment elsewhere—$20 billion overall—and no disclosed viewing figures.
items.title: Netflix hires ex-Apple exec for podcast push amid layoffs

items.summary: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff, securing a fourth non-consecutive term with more than 64 million votes against Bolsonaro's just under 60 million. Lawmaker André Janones' WhatsApp channel 'Lula's Army' drew nearly 11 million people to campaign online. Rival Flávio Bolsonaro and US president Donald Trump allege the vote was rigged, though overturning it requires evidence of fraud affecting Lula's 4.4-million-vote margin before certification on December 18.
items.title: WhatsApp Channel Lula's Army Boosted Brazil Election Comeback

items.summary: Microsoft announced a voluntary exit programme for eligible employees across India, the US, the UK and Canada on Monday, according to a blog post by the company. Globally around 60,000 employees are eligible, though Microsoft said there is no immediate clarity on how many of its about 23,000 Indian staff qualify. The offer targets level 70 and below in participating teams and includes one month's base salary per completed year of service plus health insurance and career transition services. Chief People Officer Amy Coleman described it as a time-limited initiative giving employees flexibility while letting businesses adjust their workforce. A Microsoft spokesperson reaffirmed continued investment in India, citing USD 20.5 billion committed between 2025 and 2029. Eligible staff will receive emails with terms by December 1.
items.title: Microsoft Opens Voluntary Exit Offer in Four Countries

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed Uttar Pradesh police to pay Rs 6 lakh compensation to a man wrongly held as an undertrial for six years without evidence. A bench of J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran called the probe slipshod, noting he was never named in the FIR but made an accused from CCTV footage alone. The court said investigations should be handed to the CBI if state police cover up cases.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders Compensation for Wrongful Uttar Pradesh Detention

items.summary: Lawrence Bishnoi has reportedly been moved to “Do sau kholi,” a high-security block at Ahmedabad’s Sabarmati Central Jail housing 200 dangerous inmates, sources say. The block runs four segregated sections of 50 prisoners each, with his cell roughly 7.5x11 ft. Investigators report zero direct calls from him over the past two years, though his syndicate reportedly continues operating through a shadow cabinet abroad.
items.title: Bishnoi Shifted to High-Security Sabarmati Block

items.summary: India and Mexico will sign terms of reference this week to launch negotiations for a preferential trade agreement, officials familiar with the details said. The deal aims to shield Indian exports of automobiles, textiles, footwear, plastic, steel, chemicals and toys from high tariffs up to 50% imposed by the Mexican government on about 1,463 items. Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal is visiting Mexico as part of a week-long trade mission covering both Mexico and Brussels.
items.title: India and Mexico Open Trade Negotiations

items.summary: The arrest of DMK leader and former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh has triggered protests, with MLA Sekar Babu demonstrating at the commissioner's office. The DMK called it a political vendetta ahead of the Trichy East by-election. Administration alleges he collected nearly 400 crore rupees in bribes from over 2,000 private schools and trusts for permanent recognition, while the Central Crime Branch says it has evidence tracing the money trail.
items.title: DMK Protests Anbil Mahesh Arrest in Bribery Case

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department says very severe cyclonic storm Arnab will likely cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam in Puducherry. IMD's latest bulletin at about 9:45 am Tuesday placed it roughly 260 km southeast of Vishakhapatnam. Maximum sustained windspeed is forecast at 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph by the forenoon of October 28, though a Disaster Management Authority warned coastal wind speeds could reach 90-100 kmph before landfall intensifies them.
items.title: IMD Warns Cyclone Arnab Landfall Near Yanam Coast

items.summary: Cyclone Arnab has intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal and is expected to make landfall along eastern India on October 18. The name was proposed by Bangladesh and reflects its position next on the North Indian Ocean list, where each participating country contributes names in rotation. According to IMD protocols, naming begins once winds reach at least 34 knots (about 62 kmph). Meteorological experts note that a cyclone's name has no bearing on its intensity or destination; short, distinctive labels help authorities issue warnings and evacuation orders.
items.title: Cyclone Arnab Intensifies as Very Severe Storm Heading for India's Coast

items.summary: Authorities in Andhra Pradesh’s Bapatla district temporarily closed Chirala Vodarevu, Ramapuram and Potti Subbaiahpalem beaches from Monday as a precaution against Cyclone Arnab. Officials advised tourists—especially those arriving from Hyderabad and other states—to avoid the coast until further notice. A police picket was posted to prevent entry, with access remaining barred until fresh official orders are issued.
items.title: Bapatla Beaches Closed Ahead of Cyclone Arnab

items.summary: Heavy rain and strong winds are affecting parts of Srikakulam district while a severe cyclonic storm remains centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal. Rainfall has been reported across several mandals, with light rain in others. A control room was set up at the district collectorate to coordinate response measures and address public concerns.
items.title: Srikakulam District Braces for Severe Cyclonic Storm Impact

items.summary: A new documentary, Libby de Liberdade by Anjali Monteiro and KP Jayasankar, revisits the life of 102-year-old Libia Lobo Sardesai. Built around a mural marking her birth centenary in 2024, the 79-minute film screens on October 30 at Mumbai’s Prithvi Theatre by the Vikalp collective. It centers on interviews with Lobo Sardesai and footage of her achievements as a lawyer, bank founder and radio activist.
items.title: Documentary honors Goa liberation activist Libia Lobo Sardesai

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued a very heavy rainfall alert across Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal as Severe Cyclonic Storm Arnab moves toward landfall near Yanam by Wednesday morning (October 28). The cyclone is travelling at about 25 km/h over the past six hours. IMD forecasts yellow alerts in several districts of Andhra Pradesh, an orange alert across Puri, Malkangiri, Rayagada, Ganjam, Koraput and Gajapati, a red alert on October 28, and yellow alerts covering much of Odisha's coastal districts including Nabarangapur, Nuapatna, Balangir, Kalahandi, Kandhamal, Boudh, Nayagarh, Khordha, Cuttack, Jagatsinghpur, Baleswar, Kendujhar, Mayurbhanj, Kendrapara and Jajpur. No major warning was issued in Telangana, Gujarat or Kerala, while very heavy rain is expected in Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh on October 29-30. The department warns of damage to trees, crops and vulnerable structures, plus flooding, waterlogging and possible localised landslides, and advises people to monitor updates and move to safer places if conditions worsen.
items.title: IMD Issues Heavy Rainfall Alerts Ahead of Cyclone Arnab

items.summary: India opposes UN Security Council reform that would add permanent members without veto powers, saying it undermines equality and places new members in a 'second-class' position. Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni stated all permanent members must retain the veto while it exists. India also seeks a non-permanent seat for 2028-29, contesting the sole Asia-Pacific Group spot against Tajikistan.
items.title: India Demands Veto Rights for New Permanent Council Members

items.summary: A Delhi special executive magistrate issued a notice requiring student leader Neha Bora to furnish a Rs 10,000 peace bond with one surety during an inquiry into whether her conduct may disturb public peace. The Delhi High Court declined to quash the notice on October 23, finding sufficient material and directing that police evidence be disclosed before any security is imposed. In an article for The Indian Express, Bora questioned what peacefulness means when dissenters are dispersed or silenced. Legal analysis notes the bond does not require a conviction and may last up to one year under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, while Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) protect protest rights; the inquiry must assess necessity rather than treat participation as conclusive. The case echoes similar proceedings against leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who executed bonds of Rs 50,000 after detention on October 10.
items.title: Delhi Court Upholds Notice for Student Leader's Peace Bond Amid Free-Speech Concerns

items.summary: In Sarsuna, near Kolkata, an 18-year-old youth was allegedly caught kissing his 13-year-old girlfriend on October 25. His father and a 19-year-old friend were reportedly detained at the girl's home, beaten, and forced to parade naked about 50 metres under threat of guns, according to police officer Kunal Aggarwal. Three people have been arrested; others remain at large.
items.title: Father and Son Paraded Naked in Kolkata Over Kiss With Minor

items.summary: Seventeen remand prisoners escaped from Thekkampatti sub-jail near Andipatti in Theni district on Monday night after allegedly assaulting warders. Inmates reportedly called the duty warder claiming an epileptic seizure, prompting staff to open the cell; prisoners then attacked and fled around 11 pm. Police have apprehended four, with a search underway for the remaining 13.
items.title: 17 Prisoners Escape Tamil Nadu Jail After Faking Medical Emergency

items.summary: The Jordanian air force carried out strikes in Syria, according to Jordanian state media reported by the AP on Monday. The operation reportedly killed and wounded members of armed groups and destroyed their vehicles following Friday's attack on a church in Karak, Jordan. State media did not specify which groups were targeted or where the strikes occurred.
items.title: Jordanian Air Force Strikes Syria After Karak Church Attack

items.summary: According to StockEdge's technical scan data, eight stocks in the Nifty200 pack had closing prices that crossed above their 200-day moving averages on October 26, 2026. The 200-day moving average is a trend indicator traders use; when a stock stays above it on the daily timeframe, it typically signals an overall uptrend.
items.title: Eight Nifty200 Stocks Cross Above Their 200-Day Moving Averages
